values.note: Hill County park permit: Day Permit $15 per day (noon to noon); Annual Permit $95 (May 1 - April 30); Golden Pass annual permit for 65 and older $60. Permits sold online, at self-pay boxes in the park and at Havre businesses. Reservable group campgrounds $432 a non-holiday weekend, $648 a holiday weekend, $140.40 a weekday night.

fees.source: https://www.bcpark.org/camping ('Day Permit: $15 per day (a day is from noon until noon the next day.)', 'Annual Permit: $95 (year is May 1 to April 30)', 'Golden Pass Annual Permit for those 65 years or older: $60', group rates; page footer (c) 2026), read 2026-10-22

hookups.source: https://www.bcpark.org/camping ('Beaver Creek Park only has rustic and primitive camping: NO individual hook-ups, no water, no sewer, no power'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: Picnic table, fire pit or ring and trash cans at sites; an outhouse within walking distance of most. Potable water fill stations in front of the park office; RV dump near mile marker 18 in the middle of the park.

facilities.source: https://www.bcpark.org/camping ('no internet ... no provided amenities', 'We do provide a picnic table, firepit or fire ring, trash cans, and there is an outhouse within walking distance of most sites') + https://www.bcpark.org/about-beaver-creek-park ('an RV dump site is located in the middle of the park by mile mark 18. Potable water fill stations are located in front of the park office.'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: The 100+ individual sites are not reservable: 'self-filled on a first come-first served basis' with a valid park permit. Only the large group campgrounds (pink with an asterisk on the park map) can be reserved, by the whole weekend, online or through the park office. Campers may stay 14 days on a site in any 30-day period.

booking.source: https://www.bcpark.org/camping ('Most of the campgrounds and campsites in the Park are not reservable, and self-filled on a first come-first served basis. There are over 100 of these sites, and to use them you need a valid Park Permit', 'special campgrounds that can be reserved for larger group activities') + https://www.bcpark.org/park-rules ('Parking campers, trailers and other vehicles is limited to a maximum of 14 days on a site in any 30 day period'), read 2026-10-22

note: Hill County park south of Havre in the Bears Paw Mtns - largest county park in the US (~10,000 acres) framing 17 mi of Hwy 234/Beaver Creek Rd. 100+ rustic drive-in campsites spread along the creek and its lakes, most of them on the south end of the park; a current park permit is required. Beaver Creek Reservoir/First Lake (north entrance; no wake, 10 hp) and Bear Paw Lake/Second Lake (center, boat launch) on-park. Cattle graze the park after Labor Day. --Claude
